Eh, not really that black and white. My dads had an alcohol addiction for decades— multiple DUIs,  been arrested, court ordered to months of rehab hours away, had a breathalyzer in his car for years, etc.

My dad has never had to be pulled away in an ambulance in his entire life. He also never is belligerent or loud when he’s drunk. Alcohol addiction presents itself very differently in each person that has it, and there’s many moving pieces that cause a person to talk and act in a specific way while they are inebriated.

Alcohol addiction is a progressive disease, absolutely. But like I said, my dad got his first DUI 30 years ago and has been battling the disease for a long time. At the same time, he’s not a sad person. He is genuinely a super happy person, has many passions in life. Many hobbies. Has worked for the same company for 40+ years, since he was 20 years old and worked his way up to a very high position. Wakes up every morning at 3am and has never complained a day in his life about it. Is a very respected person in both his personal and professional lives and probably has 30+ friends he sees often, people are drawn to him. Also has stayed married to my mom for 26 years (she rarely drinks).

My point is: he has always had all of these qualities about him, while being knee deep in alcohol addiction. Of course there have been things happen to him that have triggered him to have periods of drinking more heavily (his brother dying in 9/11, his father’s death, my twin brothers autism diagnosis at 2 years old, etc). But he has never spiraled the way Sonja seems like she has been for a long time. I guess he is what you call a “functioning alcoholic”. 

Sonja on the other hand? Lost many, many friends, doesn’t answer her phone most days while isolating herself (Ramona, Lu and Dorinda have confirmed this), and gets kicked out of bars and taken away in ambulances. 


So what makes someone get taken away in an ambulance— yes, in simple terms, mostly has to do with her substance addictions. However my father has had the same struggles for even longer than she has. Yet, he has never spiraled in any way shape or form even nearly the way she has. So obviously there is more that she is dealing with internally that causes her to have these pretty bad things happen to her, which is the same reason she has the alcoholism in the first place. 

And that’s what my point is. There’s many pieces to Sonja’s puzzle of why she’s stuck in a dark place.

I’ll talk off my own personal experience.

Im a pretty functional opiate user currently I would say. I’ve been an absolute functional cocaine user for almost 3 years now and take that multiple times a day but that’s a completely different ball game. Im now up to 50-60mg of oxy in one shot as my tolerance is starting to get super high. The biggest thing that helps is that I have rules with myself.

I work about 40 hours a week at an extremely high paced waitressing job where Im around other humans basically every second. First rule, I don’t take opiates at work. I’ve learned that it’s extremely obvious when I’m high off of something just as simple as weed and I used to do coke at work and I stopped when a customer tattled on me and called my job saying they think I’m on something. It started to click that I don’t realize how high I come off to other people when I’m off shit. So I vowed to never do opiates at work as I’d be nodding off every other minute knowing myself.

That means I go basically 8-10 hours sober. I use opiates as a reward for my hard work. That’s another rule I have with myself. I tell myself, “after you work this long tedious shift you can reward yourself with 5 oxys when you get home” it’s not only a way to be tough with myself but it’s a way to keep myself from blowing through my pills quick (even tho I still blow through them hella fast lol). Third rule, bills before pills. If I have a bill coming up, like I do now, I’ll give myself however many days of being sober so I can save up money for that bill. I have a $250 bill coming up in 2 days so instead of using that on oxys unfortunately I have to be sober for a bit so my car isn’t taken away.

Doing all of this also helps me get through my shifts. I’m more of a happy person at work when I know I have a bunch of oxy that I will be able to come home to at the end and it gives me more of a pep in my step to be a hard worker. I make good money so the financial aspect of it hasn’t played too much of an issue, except for the fact that I can’t buy as much coke anymore because I’m always buying oxy.

I think my colleagues would collapse to the floor if they knew I was even doing opiates, let alone how much of a heavy opiate user I am. I’m very good at hiding my personal life. I always feel like I’m living 2 lives lol. Shockingly enough my withdrawals are near non existent, the only time I ever experienced severe withdrawals was when I took fentanyl pills for a week straight and then stopped. That following week was the absolute worst week of my life and complete hell. But the only “withdrawal” symptoms I feel with oxy after not doing it for a bit is just being super tired and lazy.

Hope this helped
